items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Terminology 117:1
items.html: (To the question) What is the lower Partzuf being half of the upper? The root of this matter is in the Nekudim: at the time that the lower Hey ascended to the eyes, every degree was therefore divided into two. For the lower Hey ascended to the eyes, which is Hochma, and the degree ended there because of it, and the AHP went out and became a lower degree, as the Rav said above, page 432, item 44: that in the eyes was made the aspect of the last Hey, and YHV in the AHP. See there. Meaning that the AHP received a lower degree in YHV. As said there. And it is known that also the five Partzufim of Atzilut were all corrected in the aspect of the Malchut of the second restriction, as above in Part 13. Therefore it is discerned that every lower one is half a Partzuf of the upper one, namely the aspect of its AHP, for the AHP of the upper are always found in the GAR and eyes of the lower. And were it not for this knowledge in its clarity, there is no understanding in the Rav's discourses on ABYA, not even in a single word. And therefore he warns about this and says: “and this is a great rule, with which you will understand everything”. (Item 61).
